item.text: The mapper schema accepted the datasets but rejected the first conditional-parameter encoding before submission. I’m correcting the Galaxy-native parameter paths and will then inspect mapping quality before counting contigs.
Galaxy is still building the temporary Bowtie2 index and aligning the 40,000 reads. The job remains in its blocking execution call, so I’m letting it finish without resubmitting.

The alignment call is still active after several minutes; no failure or terminal state has been returned. I’m continuing to wait on the same job as required, then I’ll use its mapping report to decide whether per-contig counts are reliable.

Galaxy still reports the same blocking run as in progress. I’m preserving the single submission and waiting; duplicating it could create conflicting outputs and would not improve the scientific result.
The Galaxy execution remains queued/running with no terminal response. I’ll keep waiting on this exact call; once it completes, the remaining idxstats step should be quick.
No terminal state yet, but the blocking call is healthy and has not returned an error. I’m continuing the required wait without starting any duplicate analysis.
Galaxy is taking unusually long on the index-build/alignment stage, likely due to queueing rather than dataset size. The same execution remains active, and I’ll keep it as the authoritative run.
Still waiting on Galaxy’s single submitted run; there is no failure signal to act on. I’ll proceed immediately to contig counts when it reaches a terminal state.

The Galaxy backend remains the only bottleneck; the job has not returned a terminal result. I’m continuing the same blocking wait in short intervals so the run remains reproducible and compliant with the requested environment.
The same Galaxy run is still active with no error output. I’m not switching methods mid-run because the requested analysis must be completed and checked in Galaxy.
Galaxy has still not produced a terminal state. I’m continuing to wait on the original submission; the analysis and acceptance check remain pending until that returns.
The Galaxy backend continues to hold the alignment in its blocking call without failure. I’m keeping the single run active and will not infer proportions until Galaxy returns the mapping evidence.
Still no terminal response from Galaxy. The original alignment submission remains active; I’m continuing the mandated wait and preserving it as the only analysis run.
Galaxy remains queued/running with no terminal output. I’m holding to the requested execution protocol and waiting on the same call before any downstream count step.

The completed run failed its provenance check: Galaxy silently retained the built-in-reference default, so I’m rejecting that output. I’m now resolving the conditional reference input explicitly before rerunning; no proportions will be taken from the invalid BAM.
